attempts.summary: Used Ansible from the control node (node4) to configure VyOS node1 as router between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b), assigning static addresses (10.50.10.1/10.50.20.1 on node1's eth1/eth2, 10.50.10.2 on node2, 10.50.20.2 on node3) and peer routes. Installed a persistent `tc tbf` 1Mbit/s egress cap on node2's lan-a interface (enp8s0) via an Ansible-deployed NetworkManager dispatcher script plus immediate application, leaving node3's egress (and node2's ingress) unshaped. Verified with iperf3/http throughput tests: node2->node3 measured ~0.96 Mbit/s, node3->node2 unrestricted. All 4 managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms, with changed boot_id proven on each, and post-restart re-verification confirmed the VyOS routing config (saved to config.boot), the static addressing, the routes, and the tc tbf shaping all survived reboot, with end-to-end ping and Ansible connectivity restored.
